title: Where is it? The place words again

sections.title: The noun stays as it is
sections.content: You know the place words *alatt* (under), *fölött* (above), *előtt* (in front of), *mögött* (behind), *mellett* (next to) and *között* (between). They come after the noun, and the noun does not change: no *-t*, no *-ban*. Put *a* or *az* before the noun as usual: *A kutya a pad alatt van.* (The dog is under the bench.) The words stand at the end of the place phrase, before *van*.

sections.title: Between needs two
sections.content: *Között* usually has two things (or a plural): *A kutya a pad és a fa között van.* One noun with *között* means among a group, so use it with *és* and two nouns for now.

items.spanish: A kutya a pad alatt van.
items.english: The dog is under the bench.

items.spanish: A macska a kapu előtt van.
items.english: The cat is in front of the gate.

items.spanish: A madár a fa fölött van.
items.english: The bird is above the tree.

items.spanish: A kutya a lépcső mögött van.
items.english: The dog is behind the stairs.

items.spanish: A kutya a pad és a fa között van.
items.english: The dog is between the bench and the tree.

sections.content: Do not add a case ending to the noun: *a pad alatt*, not *a padban alatt*. The place word does the job of the ending.
